title: Planting Acorns

readiness.math: equal spacing with a non-standard unit; counting equal groups
readiness.reading: pre-reader friendly; all text can be read aloud

intro.speaker: miriam
intro.text: These acorns fell from the big oak. Every one could become a great tree, if it has room to grow.

intro.speaker: miriam
intro.text: Use the stick to space the holes, starting from the stone. Then two acorns in each hole, in case one doesn't sprout.

steps.speaker: miriam
steps.prompt: Put a peg one stick away from the stone. Then one stick away from that peg, and so on.
steps.hint: Lay the stick next to the stone. Where does the other end reach? Put a peg there.

feedback.placed_all: Now let's check with the stick. Does it fit each space?
feedback.crowded: Look: the stick covers a peg there. Those trees would be too close. Can that peg move further away?
feedback.far: Look: there's a gap past the end of the stick. Can that peg move closer?
feedback.all_good: Every space is one stick long.

steps.speaker: miriam
steps.prompt: Now two acorns in each hole. Count as you drop them in: one, two.
steps.hint: Find a hole with an empty little dip and put an acorn there.

older.prompt: Three acorns in each hole this time. There are no little dips: count them yourself.

feedback.full: That hole has its acorns. Try a hole with an empty dip.

outro.speaker: miriam
outro.text: Now we tuck them in. An oak grows so slowly: these will be great trees when you are grown up!

outro.speaker: miriam
outro.text: Let's put a little stick by each one, so we remember where they are.

journal_line: I planted acorns in a row in the grove. One day they will be oak trees.
unavailable_text: The acorns are planted. Now they need time, lots of time.
